items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Bob Chester, who I also played in his band

ctx.x: You were mentioning Charlie Spivak as one of your first kind of steady things. Did you get an assignment from him every week that they told you what tunes they wanted?

Occasionally. He was the second one. At first I arranged for Charlie Barnet’s band and then I sat in the sax section for a while. So he was the first guy that kept calling me to write things for the band. Charlie would leave some stuff up to me. Original material that I wanted to write he would put into the book. Occasionally — song pluggers in those days were very big. And so Charlie would call and say call so-and-so at Robbins Music or something, and he’s got a couple of tunes that he’d like you to look at. And…
The tunes that came out back then that the song pluggers pushed, a lot of them seemed to have a verse that we never heard.
